BREAKING: The number of restaurants in New York dropped ~2,000 YoY in Q1 2026, posting its largest YoY decline in at least 36 years.

This surpasses even the worst contraction recorded in any quarter during the 2020 pandemic.

The number of eating and drinking places in New York State has now declined YoY for 4 consecutive quarters, its longest streak since 2021.

This comes as restaurants are facing surging operating expenses, including insurance premiums, wages, interest rates, utilities, and health coverage, with overall costs rising faster than national averages.

Last year, employee health insurance costs jumped +12.9% for New York-area service firms, business insurance rose +7.0%, while utility costs surged +8.5%, according to the Manhattan Chamber of Commerce.

Skyrocketing costs are crushing New York restaurants.

Non-asset owners are seeing a large drop in US consumer sentiment.

Since January 2026, consumer sentiment is down -27% among the bottom 33% of stockholders, the largest decline among the stock-wealth groups surveyed.

This is followed by those who do not own stocks, whose sentiment is down -25% over the same period.

By comparison, sentiment is down just -9% among the middle 33% and -7% among the top 33% of stockholders.

Asset ownership has helped offset the impact of higher living costs, leaving consumers with fewer or no stocks more exposed to the recent acceleration in inflation.

Meanwhile, 1-year consumer inflation expectations rose +0.1 percentage point this month, to 4.7%, its 2nd-highest reading since August 2025.

Own assets or be left behind.

Large US bank stocks are under historic pressure:

The KBW Bank Index has dropped for 6 consecutive weeks, its longest streak since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

This also marks its 3rd-longest streak this century.

Over this span, the index has fallen -11%, to its lowest level since the first week of June.

Bank of America, $BAC, State Street, $STT, and Citigroup, $C, were among the worst performers over this period, declining -18%, -14%, and -10%, respectively.

This comes amid rising investor concerns over AI disrupting financial services and higher interest rate expectations.

Furthermore, mixed Q3 2026 earnings results reported last week failed to ease the pressure.

Large US bank stocks are having a terrible year.

BREAKING: Interest expense on US public debt rose +$144 billion YoY in FY2026, or +12%, to a record $1.36 trillion.

This marks the 6th consecutive annual increase, for a total of +$839 billion, or +161%.

For perspective, total receipts rose just +3.2% YoY, to $5.40 trillion.

In other words, interest on federal debt accounted for 25% of total US government receipts.

Meanwhile, Social Security, the largest government expense, jumped +$86 billion YoY, or +5.5%, to a record $1.67 trillion.

At this pace, interest costs will exceed Social Security as the largest government outlay by the end of 2028.

What is the long-term plan here?

With H&S patterns low of the right shoulder is the swing low and the level for negation. It can serve as the pattern negation level for H&S bottom after the breakout of the neckline or

It can act as the short signal level if the H&S bottom fails with a breakdown below the swing low.  

This is how I analyzed the chart on the 1st breakout signal. $BTC

$BTC The swing low inside the wide rectangle range can be utilized as a vide stop for the signal at 82.8K.

Note that recently there has been 2 breakout signals based on well-defined technical levels.

1) Breakout above 67.2K (completion of the H&S bottom)
2) Breakout above horizontal boundary of the rectangle (completion of the rectangle as a bottom reversal)

On the second one we are experiencing a hard re-test.  $BTC
